# Changelog
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.3.2] - 2022-06-04
### Added
- Added `CKDBRecordFieldValue` convenience factory functions rooted
  at `CKRecordFieldValue.make`.
  For example, to create an encrypted `Int64` list value, you can do:
  `const fieldValue = CKRecordFieldValue.make.encrypted.list.int64([123])` or
  `const fieldValue = CKRecordFieldValue.make.list.encrypted.int64([123])`.
  An unencrypted `Int64` can be made like this:
  `const fieldValue = CKRecordFieldValue.make.int64(123)`.
- `makeRecordFieldValue` is an alias for `CKRecordFieldValue.make`.
- TypeScript: `CKRecordFieldValue` has type aliases:
  For example, to reference `CKDBRecordFieldEncryptedInt64ListValue`, you can do:
  `CKRecordFieldValue.Encrypted.List.Int64` or
  `CKRecordFieldValue.List.Encrypted.Int64`.

### Changed
- TypeScript: Removed generic parameter from `CKDBRecordFieldValue`.
- Promise functions now take a single options parameter and returns
  a function that takes a single end point parameters object and
  returns the promise. This enables currying of the promise
  functions so that you can bind an options object to the function.
  Example:
  ```
  // Calling the promise function.
  const containers1 = await getContainersP({configuration, security})(params);

  // A function with a bound options object.
  export const getContainers =
    getContainersP({configuration, security});

  // Invoking the bound function.
  const containers2 = await getContainers(params);
  ```
- Enumerations whose values had underscores in them should've had
  underscores in their enumeration keys. This has been fixed.
  Any enumerations that were used in existing
  code may break. For example, 
  `CKDBRecordReferenceAction.DELETESELF` is now
  `CKDBRecordReferenceAction.DELETE_SELF`.
